[AGENT 5 REVISION 2026-09-20] CFR VERIFIED BY AGENT 5 (mission item d). The WER 'Diseases Subject to the Regulations' table prints cases and deaths as two adjacent columns on the SAME row, for the SAME place and the SAME period string, so the numerator and denominator here do share a denominator and a period by construction - this is not a cumulative-deaths-over-weekly-cases error, which is the usual cause of an implausible CFR in this dataset. The high ratio is a small-denominator artefact compounded by reporting lag: a death notified in week W frequently belongs to a case counted in week W-1 or W-2, so a WEEKLY CFR on a denominator under 50 is not an estimate of case fatality and should not be read as one. For scale, Ghana's WHO annual CFRs over this era are 4.9% (1971), 5.1% (1972), 5.8% (1973), 6.5% (1978) and 11.1% (1982). Confidence is already at 0.70 and is left there.
